thread:
ryan: Heads-up — we’re seeing a sharp increase in connection resets from edge-proxies in us-east-2. Symptoms: model pull failures, 502s on short lived upstream connections, and high TIME_WAIT counts on NAT paths.

marta: seeing the same in graphs. CPU on edge proxies is fine, but ephemeral port exhaustion on the VPC side looks suspicious. 

ryan: paste of `ss` output from one affected NAT instance:```netstat -an | grep TIME_WAIT | wc -l
120412```and `ss -tan state TIME-WAIT` shows thousands from 10.0.3.* -> S3/model-host ranges.

olivia: are these model pulls from node bootstraps or live inference fanout?

ryan: mostly model pulls during autoscaling spikes + periodic cache refresh. One batch job at 03:00 caused a big fanout. Each pull opens new outbound connection to model registry (S3 over internet).

sam: immediate mitigations we should try: 1) add a second NAT gateway in the AZ + update route table to spread egress, 2) enable S3 VPC endpoints to avoid NAT for model pulls, 3) reduce concurrency of model puller.

marta: +1 on S3 endpoint — that will short-circuit the majority of bytes. We should also enable longer keepalives/connection pooling on the puller so subsequent pulls reuse sockets instead of opening N new connections.

infra-bot: Incident INC-4231 created: "us-east-2 outbound socket churn — ephemeral port shortage" assigned to eng-infra.

olivia: short-term: I'll spin up a lightweight NAT instance ASG in the AZ to soak connections while we provision a second managed NAT gateway. That should lower port reuse pressure.

ryan: can we throttle model pull concurrency by cluster-nodes-per-minute? We should avoid all nodes pulling simultaneously after scale-out. Add jitter and backoff to the bootstrap script.

sam: logging observation: many connections are to third-party telemetry endpoints as well. We should audit egress hosts and add VPC endpoints or proxy them through a pooled connection.

marta: note for runbook: increase ephemeral port range on Linux (`net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range`) is an option but it only delays exhaustion and can cause other issues. Prefer reducing fanout + use VPC endpoints + split NAT.

olivia: deploying S3 endpoint policy and updating bootstrap to use parallelism=2 then ramp to 6 over 10m. Deploying now.

ryan: evidence: after temporarily reducing bootstrap parallelism on one batch we saw TIME_WAIT drop ~40% within 90s. Good sign.

sam: follow-ups: (1) create quota docs for model-puller concurrency, (2) add a per-AZ NAT capacity metric to console, (3) automate canary of S3 endpoint for model pulls.

marta: long term: consider an internal model-cache service in each AZ that keeps warm models and serves nodes over HTTP/keepalive so only the cache fetches externally. That reduces global egress fanout.

ryan: agreed. For now: olivia, proceed with NAT instance + S3 endpoint + bootstrap throttle. I'll update INC-4231 with mitigation steps and postmortem checklist. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: Deployment note: `route-table/us-east-2a` updated to include NAT instance (eni-0abc) at 1990054670.

olivia: NAT instance is up; monitoring ephemeral port counts across AZs. Early metrics show drop in per-NAT TIME_WAIT by ~30%. Will keep watch and patch bootstrap across autoscaler groups.

ryan: thanks team. After stable for 2h we'll promote changes to staging and schedule a remediation retro. :eyes:
